News.title: Six children among eight family members killed in ‘suspicious’ house fire as arson investigators scour scene
News.content:
BLAZE TRAGEDY Six children among eight family members killed in ‘suspicious’ house fire as arson investigators scour scene

SIX children are among eight family members who have been killed in a “suspicious” house fire in Michigan.

Cops are now probing whether the tragedy was a murder-suicide after some of the victims were found with gunshot wounds.



The children ranged in age from around five to 15 years old, according to Captain Jacob Sparks of the Ottawa County Sheriff’s Office.

Police have described the incident as “suspicious”, but Sparks added it was “too early to say that it’s a murder-suicide”.



He continued: “I can tell you that that’s one theory that we have and we’re still looking to see if we can verify that.”

Sparks confirmed that some of the victims suffered gunshot wounds, although police were probing whether “other means” were involved.



“It would be premature for me to say what caused their deaths,” he said.

Sparks added that autopsies will take place on Saturday.

Firefighters were called to the house between 8.30am and 9am yesterday morning after receiving reports of a strong smell of smoke.

They scoured the area without success, but later rushed back to the scene after residents reported white smoke rising from the home on the 14900 block of Riverside Trail.



The neighbourhood where the blaze broke out appears to be an affluent area with pristine green lawns and tall trees.

It comes days after five children from the same family were killed in a horror house fire in Peru.

At least 10 people were found dead inside the home with the youngest being a three-year-old and the eldest being a 72-year-old.

The victims were all members of the same family from Lima, Peru, police chief Oscar Arriola confirmed.



Peru’s president-elect Keiko Fujimori visited the ruins as she called the deaths “a terrible massacre”.

Fire crews rushed to two homes in the southern La Victoria district early on Wednesday after witnesses recalled seeing flames coming out of the windows.

At least 17 members of the family were in the building when the fire started at 3am local time.

Seven managed to escape the blaze, reports Infobae.

Survivor Gina Vilchez told reporters she was able to save herself and her children as they ran through smoke and dodged falling charred debris.



Five children, aged three, six, six, eight and 15, were found dead after the fire was extinguished.

Five adults aged 29, 35, 42 and 72, were also recovered.

Police chief Arriola said their bodies were burned beyond recognition.

One line of inquiry behind the cause of the inferno is a possible arsonist attack by local extortionists.

A group are known to have been threatening local businesses around the same time as the deadly inferno, Peruvian media reported.



Local media say the family owned electric motorcycles and had a mattress business so may have been targeted.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Colonel John Lujan, who is leading the investigation, confirmed “a possible deliberate act or a case of extortion” is among the possible causes.

A statement from the National Police of Peru said: “Today, all of Peru falls silent in the face of a tragedy that plunges our nation into mourning.”

News.title: Teenage boy stabbed to death in ‘horrific violence’ as cops swoop on youths ‘armed with large knives’ in park
News.content:
KNIFE ATTACK Teenage boy stabbed to death in ‘horrific violence’ as cops swoop on youths ‘armed with large knives’ in park

A TEENAGE boy has tragically died after he was violently stabbed multiple times at a park.

Police responded to reports of “a number of teenagers carrying large knives” in Kingsway Recreation Ground, Luton at about 6.30pm yesterday.



The 17-year-old victim was rushed to hospital but sadly passed away.

The boy has not yet been formally identified, but his family are being supported by specially trained officers.



A murder investigation has been launched following the “horrific violence”, with one boy arrested on suspicion of violent disorder and being questioned in police custody.

Another teenager was also arrested on suspicion of violent disorder but is being treated in hospital with serious injuries.

Detectives from the Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Hertfordshire Major Crime Unit have appealed for anyone with information relating to the terrible incident to contact them immediately.

Detective Chief Inspector Nick Gardener said: “Horrific violence in Luton has sadly cost a teenage boy his life today.



“Our thoughts are first and foremost with the loved ones of the boy who lost his life in such tragic circumstances.

“Incidents such as this have a significant impact on our communities. There is currently an increased police presence in the area, and high visibility patrols will continue.

“I would urge anyone who witnessed what happened, or who has any information, to come forward and speak to police to help us bring those responsible to justice.

“We are aware that images and videos are circulating on social media. Please refrain from sharing any such footage and instead contact police.

“Not only is this material distressing for the family, but it could also form part of vital evidence in our investigation.”

News.title: Moment murderer Vickrum Digwa tells his mum to hide knife used to kill Henry Nowak
News.content:
VIDEO footage has revealed the moment murderer Vickrum Digwa told his mother to take the knife he used to kill Henry Nowak away from the crime scene.

The Crown Prosecution Service released the clip after Digwa’s mother, Kiran Kaur, was jailed for three years at Southampton crown court last Friday for assisting an offender.



In the footage taken on Digwa’s phone, which is pointed at the ground, he can be heard speaking to Kaur in Punjabi, asking her to remove the knife.

She then took it back to the family home.



Digwa, 23, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 21 years on June 1 for the murder of Henry, after falsely claiming the 18-year-old racially abused him.

Last month, The Sun revealed Nowak’s killer would have his “lenient” jail sentence reviewed after the case sparked fury across the UK.



Henry was knifed five times with a 21cm ceremonial sword by Digwa in a sick attack in Southampton last December.

Solicitor General Ellie Reeves has referred the case to the Court of Appeal under the unduly lenient scheme, saying it “horrified me”.

She said: “This case horrified me, and I know that feeling is shared by the British public.

“It is right that difficult questions need to be answered about the way the police handled Henry’s Nowak’s murder, while my role is to review Digwa’s sentence for his crimes.



“After careful consideration, I have taken the decision to refer this case to the Court of Appeal.

“No sentence can ever undo the devastation that Henry’s family have suffered, or fill the void left by his loss.

“But I hope this referral goes some way towards bringing them the justice they deserve.”



Hampshire Police is currently being investigated by the IOPC, the police watchdog, over Henry’s arrest.

News.title: Beach hero who pulled mum & daughter from water in Mersea tragedy sprang into action after seeing bodies floating
News.content:
A HERO dad dived into the sea to rescue a drowning mother and daughter after he saw bodies facedown in the waves.

Craig Bowe battled fierce tides to pull Shelina Rahman, 41, her daughter Samia, 15, and two others from the water, while also helping a seven-year-old boy.



The mum and daughter were given CPR on the beach but the pair died at the scene after they heroically tried to save the boy – thought to be a relative – themselves.

Emergency services rushed to the beach at just after 5.35pm following reports that adults and children had gotten into trouble in the water.



The boy, who had become stranded on a sandbank, was airlifted to hospital and remains in a critical condition while three others were taken by ambulance.

Craig was on a day trip for his daughter’s 10th birthday to West Mersea, near Colchester in Essex on Wednesday.





The kitchen fitter leapt into action after hearing a man call for help and seeing people unconscious in the choppy sea.

He told the BBC: “I noticed that no one else was going into the water, I am an okay swimmer, and the people needed help.”

Craig dived into the cold water and pulled Shelina from the waves before running back to rescue her daughter.

His bravery didn’t stop there and Craig returned to the sea a third time to rescue another young woman.

Finally he swam out 150 yards with life jackets and a life ring to help get the seven year-old boy onto a lifeboat, and bring another teenage boy to shore.



The boy got into difficulty after he was stranded on a sandbank and cut off from the shore, it is understood.

“I helped sort of shoo him onto the boat, because he was face down too… but the seven-year-old was not in a good way” Craig said.

He added that he was being bashed by waves as the current got stronger.



Meanwhile, his wife Carly, had called 999, and was trying to resuscitate the mum and daughter.

She humbly said: “Everybody on that beach that day played their part in giving that family the best chance they could to survive.

“Everyone really stepped up and it was incredible to see.”

Craig and Carly told The Times they had been tidying up after celebrating with their four children when they heard screaming.

The couple then saw a man calling for help as his family were stranded and struggling in the water.



Craig said he went into “autopilot” while Carly remained on the beach comforting the family members not in the water.

Their daughters Ava and Madison ran to find life jackets and rings while Craig battled increasingly dangerous conditions.

Carly said: “We don’t feel like we are heroes, we just did what was needed as the family were out for fun for the day just like us, and got caught in difficulty.



“It was a surreal experience, one I don’t want to have again. It still hasn’t sunk in as to what happened that evening.

“So many questions that we have as to how and why it happened but all our thoughts are for the family and the seven-year-old boy fighting for his life.”

The grieving dad was part of the Bangladeshi Nationalist Party’s UK wing and a leader of the Jubo Dal movement in Britain.

Dr Rahman told how his daughter had visited him earlier in the day before heading to the beach with family.

According to a relative, around ten members of the family were playing near the sea when a “big wave came in.”



Selina and her daughter Samia, who tried to rescue the struggling 7-year-old, were reportedly poor swimmers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hundreds have flocked to Brick Lane Jamme Masjid Mosque in East London to pay their tributes in the wake of the tragedy.

Essex Police have urged anyone with information to come forward by calling 101 and quoting incident 1090.

News.title: Netflix’s Toxic Love Story liar Angela Diaz’s new career revealed after 3 years in jail for elaborate cyberstalking hoax
News.content:
THE woman jailed for an elaborate cyberstalking hoax which is the focus of Netflix documentary A Toxic Love Story is now working as a counselor and claims she was wrongly convicted.

Angela Diaz, who now goes by Angi Connell — her maiden name — has moved to Arizona and built a new career.



She and her former husband were jailed for orchestrating a false rape and stalking plot to frame his ex Michelle Hadley in a bizarre case that gained national attention.

The U.S. Sun can confirm Connell is now listed online as the Director of Peer Counseling at Exhale Pro-Voice, a nonprofit that trains people to provide support through text-based services.



She offers emotional support based on shared lived experience, rather than professional clinical training.

Connell previously volunteered with the organization before moving into a leadership role and is working toward a doctorate in psychology with the goal of becoming a licensed psychologist.

The business’s website lists her as a “bisexual Peruvian-American adoptee living on the ancestral lands of the Onk Akimel O’odham and Xalchidom Piipaash peoples.”

She first discovered Exhale Pro-Voice in 2016 while “searching for a reproductive justice organization grounded in intersectionality, following her own abortion experience.”



The site adds, “After spending time in prison, Angi pursued a Master’s degree in Psychology and Justice Studies, deepening her commitment to transformative justice.”

In an interview with VoyagePhoenix last year, Connell spoke about rebuilding her life.

She claimed she had been “wrongfully convicted” and said her time in prison shaped her desire to help others.

However, there has been no court ruling overturning her conviction, and her guilty plea remains part of the official record.

The U.S. Sun could not confirm an address for her through public records, but she lists herself in Arizona on a private Instagram profile.



Her new career marks a dramatic change from her situation that made national headlines — one prosecutors described as a calculated attempt to frame another woman.

The case began in 2016 when Hadley, a California woman who had previously been in a relationship with Ian Diaz, became the target of a sick harassment campaign.

Connell, who was married to Diaz at the time, was accused of creating fake online accounts, impersonated Hadley and sent threatening messages to herself in an effort to make it appear she was stalking and threatening the couple.

The case even involved a shocking “rape fantasy” plot, where Connell framed Hadley for messaging men on Craigslist’s now-defunct “Casual Encounters” section, inviting them to come to the home she shared with Diaz to carry out violent sexual fantasies.

The situation went as far Connell calling 911 to report that she had been attacked by a masked man.



The Orange County District Attorney’s Office said Connell fabricated evidence and orchestrated the scheme in an attempt to frame Hadley and she was arrested in August 2016.

Connell pleaded guilty to multiple felony charges connected to the plot, including false imprisonment by fraud, falsely reporting a crime and stalking-related offenses.

She was sentenced to five years in prison and was released in July 2020 after serving around three years.

Since, Connell has largely stayed out of the spotlight and declined to participate in Netflix’s documentary about the case.

The bombshell series, which dropped this week, also features an interview with a former boyfriend, who revealed she lied about being pregnant with twins and having Stage 4 cancer.



A video shows her wearing a wig and being confronted by his friends and family, before she later confirmed on a phone call with police that she was never sick.

She also claimed to be a lawyer for a period, but was later exposed.

Connell spoke in-depth to VoyagePhoenix about her life behind bars.

“In 2016, I faced 23 to life charges for a crime I did not commit, and subsequently spent five years in a California prison,” she said.

She described the experience as “harrowing and tragic” and said it transformed her life.



She further explained that she completed her education in prison and insists she is more than just a felon.

Talking about her day-to-day life, she also said, “With three rescue dogs, my mornings are a crash course in patience, chaos, and unconditional love.

“My goal is to start the day tech-free — take a few deep breaths, set an intention, smile, soak up some sunshine, and hydrate like I mean it.”

Her former husband also faced federal prosecution for his role in the scheme.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Diaz, a former US Marshal, was convicted in 2023 on charges including cyberstalking, conspiracy, perjury and obstruction-related offenses linked to the plot against Hadley.



He was sentenced to more than 10 years in federal prison and remains incarcerated.

News.title: Special forces intelligence chief detained after sending pictures from a secret op to his girlfriend
News.content:
SECURITY RISK Special forces intelligence chief detained after sending pictures from a secret op to his girlfriend

A SPECIAL forces intelligence chief has been detained after sending pictures to his girlfriend from a secret mission.

The trooper, known only as Soldier A, took his personal phone on covert ops and had pictures of secret bases, prisoners of war and enemy fighters slain by his comrades.



The images were deemed “useful to an enemy” but he shared several with his lover, who was serving in the Royal Air Force.

He was convicted of sharing information useful to an enemy and negligence of duty.



Sentencing Soldier A, Judge Jane England said he risked blowing the lid on the secret foreign mission.

She said: “The location and operation were at the time secret and remained a secret.

“Phones are hacked for information. That can hurt trust between nations that the UK can and needs to rely on.”

He was arrested at Heathrow Airport and police who searched his home found six USB sticks and his phone that showed video footage of sensitive tactics, locations of operations with GPS data.

Judge England said that he left the material in his house while he went on holiday overseas.

She added: “None of the material should have been stored on your own personal device and this was done so that you had immediate access to the material for personal use.”



The experienced soldier, who was the chief of his sensitive site exploitation team, which collected intelligence after raids.

Soldier A told his partner, who was also not named, when operations were happening and where they would be happening, as well as who they were against.

The information could have damaged international relations, Bulford Military Court Martial was told.

He was arrested in January 2022 at Heathrow Airport, and his home was searched.

He was sentenced to eight months’ service detention for negligence in his performance of duty and five months’ service detention for disclosure of information useful to the enemy, to run concurrently.



Commander Edward Hannah, for the prosecution, said: “Soldier A was experienced and fully aware of the duty….there is an underlying theme to this defendant’s attitudes to this type of material and his attitude to his duty.”

In his defence Fiona Edington claimed the secret data was “chit chat” and gossip with his RAF lover.

News.title: RAF fighter jets scrambled to escort passenger plane set to land at major UK airport after flight was ‘causing concern’
News.content:
TWO RAF jets were scrambled to escort a flight heading to a major UK airport last night.

The Royal Air Force have confirmed a ”quick reaction alert” was activated as the flight was “causing concern to civil authorities”.



The incident began after Qatar Airways flight QR23 from the Qatari capital Doha to Manchester Airport entered UK airspace yesterday evening.

It is not clear what the cause for concern is about although it’s understood it was thought there was an issue with the aircraft.



Some aviation websites say that air traffic controllers lost contact with the aircraft, although this has not been confirmed.

The RAF have confirmed two Typhoon jets were sent from RAF Coningsby in Lincolnshire to escort the aircraft.



The fighter jets intercepted the Boeing 777 over Nottingham.

The escort though is thought to have been called off some time before it reached Manchester airport.



An RAF spokesperson said: “We can confirm that an RAF Quick Reaction Alert was launched for a Qatar Airways flight which was causing concern to civil authorities.

“The incident was resolved and the airliner landed safely at Manchester Airport.”

Emergency ground services were put on standby as a standard precautionary measure, but the plane taxied safely to its gate without further incident.

According to the Manchester Airport arrivals board, the flight landed at 7.45pm yesterday.

Civil aviation authorities are expected to carry out an investigation in coordination with the airline.



The Sun Online has contacted Qatar Airways for comment.

News.title: Moving Rudakubana from prison to a secure hospital despite his wicked crimes makes a mockery of the justice system
News.content:
Justice cheated

THERE is no punishment severe enough to fit the horrific crimes of Southport killer Axel Rudakubana.

So the decision to move him from prison to a secure psychiatric hospital makes a mockery of the justice system — and inflicts fresh trauma on the victims of his murderous rampage.



If the authorities had been as concerned about his mental health BEFORE the attack, three little girls who just wanted to dance would still be alive.

Yet he was discharged by a psychiatrist just three months before he went on his terrifying knife frenzy.



Now the remorseless monster has hoodwinked officials into believing he can be more safely managed in Broadmoor.

The truth is that Rudakubana is a radicalised, sadistic and highly-dangerous killer who is playing the system to secure a more cushy life in hospital.



Campaigner Emma Webber, whose son Barnaby was murdered in the Nottingham attacks, summed it up perfectly when she said: “This is an insult to the dead and a betrayal of the living.”

In a further insult to the Southport families, Rudakubana won his move from London’s Belmarsh prison just days before they mark the second anniversary of his onslaught next Wednesday.

Did anybody think to consult them first?

The convict — who last year hurled boiling water over a guard — has already shown his guile by persuading officers to return his TV and DVD privileges.



Law-abiding taxpayers will have to fork out an extra £250,000 a year for him to enjoy the freedoms of a modern, purpose-built unit with spacious natural-light wards, a central therapeutic hub and integrated physical healthcare.

It is yet another sickening example of the distorted priorities of a prison system which so often rides roughshod over the interests of crime victims to appease violent offenders.

When will our soft-touch justice system realise that not all violent criminals are mentally ill — but just plain evil.

Justice Secretary Alex Norris must demand an explanation of who approved this switch and why.

Many people think Rudakubana’s crimes were so wicked, he no longer deserves to be alive himself.



The least we can expect is that he spends the rest of his days staring at the four walls of a prison cell.

Fugitive’s let-off

LABOUR’S scheme to free convicts on to our streets was cooked up to fix the prison overcrowding crisis.

But now it’s offering a “get out of jail early” card to fugitives.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Victims of a convicted child rapist who is on the run and has never served a day behind bars have been told he will be eligible for time off his 22-year stretch — if he ever gets caught.

This is simply justice delayed — and then discounted.

News.title: Essex fire live: Inferno rages after explosion as 100 firefighters tackle flames
News.content:
Aerial images show the scale of the blaze at a farm in Essex

More than 100 firefighters are tackling a massive fire at a farm off Southend Road between East Hanningfield and Rettendon in Essex

A massive explosion at a farm in Essex has shaken buildings up to 15 miles away, with footage showing a huge fireball erupting from the site.

Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said more than 100 firefighters worked to tackle a blaze involving industrial units at a farm off Southend Road, between East Hanningfield and Rettendon, near Chelmsford, on Friday evening.

The blaze, which is understood to be at Highlands Farm, has been declared a major incident due to its size. Police have cordoned off a large area around the site.

"If you live or are travelling nearby, please continue to keep your windows and doors closed," the fire service said. "Please avoid the area while we deal with this incident."

News.title: Spain and France wildfires live: Brits among 200,000 fleeing scorched tourist areas
News.content:
More than 200,000 people in France and Spain have been evacuated as wildfires continue to tear through vast areas of both countries

Huge wildfires are ravaging parts of south-west France and central Spain, forcing the evacuation of an estimated 200,000 people - including British tourists.

French authorities have ordered the immediate evacuation of suburbs in Bordeaux - the largest city in the affected region - as the flames shift towards the area.

British families were among those evacuated from a Bordeaux hotel at 3.30am as staff warned smoke had been travelling over from the raging fires around 20-miles away in the Cap Ferret peninsula, reports MailOnline.

Around 141,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in France's Gironde and Landes departments, the French interior ministry said. Some residents and holidaymakers even fled by boat as flames swept through the popular tourist area of Cap Ferret on France's Atlantic coast.

In Spain, 60,000 have been forced to leave their homes in towns west of Madrid, the Spanish interior ministry said. Wildfires in the Madrid region and the nearby province of Ávila have prompted the government to declare a national emergency over wildfires for the first time.

Meanwhile, Police Scotland has declared a major incident as firefighters battle a huge wildfire in the Cairngorms National Park, with hundreds of people evacuated from homes in its path.

The force said strengthening winds have made the fire more unpredictable and caused it to spread towards Nethy Bridge, a small village in the Strathspey area of the park, prompting the decision to declare a major incident.

News.title: Donald Trump's wild week as tariffs return and America is terrorised by poop lettuce
News.content:
Donald Trump's wild week as tariffs return and America is terrorised by poop lettuce

Tariffs are back on the table - and this time he's using forced labour and poop lettuce as excuses. Here's everything you need to know from Trumpworld this week

View 2 Images America is being terrorised by lettuce (Image: AP Photo/Rod Lamkey)

Donald Trump continues to find new and innovative ways to threaten his global rivals. Tariffs are back on the table - and this time he's using forced labour and poop lettuce as excuses.

‌



Meanwhile he's trying to shoehorn the world's most hated man into a job at the body tasked with fostering world peace. He's slapping his name on things again - but maybe he's kind of got a point this time.

‌



And he's threatening war crimes against Iran, in what has become a distinctly costly war.

‌



Here's all the wild, alarming and downright bizarre things that happened in Trumpworld this week. Buckle up.

Infanti-no

Donald Trump is proving himself to be the world's worst job recruiter.

Not satisfied with trying to make a man who was under investigation for child sex trafficking (Matt Gaetz) his attorney general, or putting a man whose brain has been partially eaten by a parasitic worm (RFK JR) in charge of the health department Trump wants a man who is hated by literally everyone in the world to run the organisation tasked with maintaining world peace.

‌



That's right: Gianni Infantino, the infamous President of FIFA, inventor of the FIFA peace prize, should be Secretary General of the United Nations, Trump reckons.

View 2 Images I bet he'd never let the escalators break down (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Now this is never going to happen, for two important reasons. First, Infantino seems to quite like the idea of retaining his position at the top of professional football so much that he keeps adding countries to the tournament in the hope that they'll vote for him to stay.

‌



Second, the United Nations has a process for picking Secretaries General which is so complicated it would make the electoral college blush. And at the end of it, the permanent members of the security council, which includes France and the UK, get a veto. And after the World Cup exits both countries have just had, you can bet your life they'd use it.

I'm sorry, the Iran war has cost how much?

Donald Trump - and now Marco Rubio - have doubled down...or is it tripled down now? ...on their threats of war crimes against the people of Iran, warning the Islamic Republic any attacks on boats in the strait of hormuz will be responded to with bombing raids on bridges and power stations near Tehran. As we've covered before even threatening to do that is a war crime. But as we've also covered, it's literally impossible to prosecute the President of the United States for war crimes.

But the most eyebrow raising moment in the Iran war this week was secretary of war Pete Hegseth's admission that the US has already spent 37 and a half BILLION DOLLARS on the conflict. And with no end in sight, you can perhaps understand why Trump is getting quite so tetchy when he's asked what the plan is.

‌



And it doesn't end there. Hegseth made the admission at a senate hearing where he was asking for MORE MONEY. Like a permatanned Oliver Twist he went cap in hand to congress demanding another $70 billion more to fund the war and replenish depleted weapons stocks - even warning troops could end up going without pay if Congress refused to stump up the eye watering bonus.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Trump swerves question about war crimes

While Trump seems to be perfectly comfortable making the threat of war crimes, he's less keen on acknowledging that what he's doing is a war crime.

Asked about it in the Oval Office on Friday, he refused to say whether he thought attacking infrastructure was a war crime, turning his fire on the reporter who asked the question. Again.

Make America Poop Again

There's no way to sugar coat this. America is in the middle of a pooping epidemic.

‌



An outbreak of cyclospora was linked to rogue lettuce in Taco Bells in Pennsylvania and beyond. This has been - sorry - bubbling for a couple of weeks so far. So you'd think Trump would havem ore to say about it.

Asked when it would be safe to eat lettuce again, Trump said last night that his government is "going to put a major tariff on tax on Mexico because of the **lettuce**."

He wants to name another thing after himself

From an early age, Donald Trump longed to have things named after him. From Trump Tower, vodka and frozen steak, and then in office the peace institute, Trump Accounts, Trump RX, and (sigh) the Kennedy Centre and Palm Beach Airport, he's slapped his name around like a cat marking territory.

‌



The latest? Penn Station in New York City. Now, in this case there is actually a case to be made for changing the name, because there's also a Penn Station in New Jersey, and another in Baltimore. And it's pretty confusing.

But there's no rule that says everything that gets re-named during a President's term in office means they have to be named after him.

Tariffs are back baybee

Trump's grabbed hold of his favourite stick to wave at other countries again this week - Tariffs.

‌



And the timing is no coincidence. Trump's global 10% tariffs expired at midnight on Friday. And Trump has been casting about for excuses to slap replacement tariffs on as many countries as possible.

For example Canada is being threatened with tariffs because of the wildfires blowing smoke south of the border. Some 60 major trading partners - including the UK - are being threatened with tariffs over "forced labour" practices.

And now, yes, he says he's slapping tariffs on Mexico because that's where the poop lettuce came from.

Article continues below

It is worth remembering that Trump's entire tariff regime was struck down as spurious by the Supreme Court, and this is a clear attempt to circumvent that ruling. Trump has said as much. There is every chance that these tariffs never get enacted.

News.title: New nail gel ban 'already in force' as August change also planned across the UK
News.content:
New nail gel ban 'already in force' as August change also planned across the UK

Big change for the rules for salon and at-home products amid health concerns over ingredients

View Image Health concerns from chemicals are behind a new ban with rules coming in August and some already in force in July (Image: Getty)

New nail gel ban comes into force in August across the UKThe UK cosmetics industry has issued an update as new bans have already come into effect on the use of nail gels in the UK. Millions every week get regular treatments in high streets around the UK, but most don’t realise big changes are coming in with some already in force.

‌



The first changes were introduced on July 15 and further ingredient bans and concentration limits following on August 15, 2026, Professional Beauty reported.

‌



The first changes came into force on July 15, 2026, banning the UV filter 4-MBC in newly placed cosmetic products and lowering the threshold at which products containing formaldehyde-releasing preservatives must carry a warning.

‌



Further rules will take effect on August 15, 2026, including a ban on TPO in newly placed cosmetic products and new maximum concentration limits for the fragrance ingredient Hexyl Salicylate. Scientists have also identified the chemical as a possible cause of skin sensitisation. Therefore, repeatedly exposing your skin to uncured gel products increases your risk of developing an allergy.

The beauty publication said: “For most salon owners, therapists and nail technicians, the practical takeaway is to check professional nail stock for TPO, ask suppliers to confirm that products comply with the new rules and keep purchase and batch records for affected products.”

The new guidelines are merely a component of new UK Cosmetic Safety Regulations that have changed the process for manufacturers and importers who wish to continue selling certain types of gel nail products in the UK. For most consumers, the changes will occur quietly in the background.

‌



All you need to know about new nail gel ban coming to UK in August READ MORE :

Danielle Louise, beauty expert at Fresha, said.”If you regularly get gel nails, there’s no reason to cancel your appointments or worry that something has suddenly become unsafe,’ she says. ‘The vast majority of professional salons use trusted brands that keep up to date with cosmetic regulations, and many manufacturers have already introduced reformulated products well ahead of the deadline.”

The change was highlighted in a written answer to a question at the House of Lords. Baroness Bennett of Manor Castle asked the government: “What plans they have to ban the use of the chemical trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide in gel nail polish, following the decision of the EU to do so.”

It was answerered: “Trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide (TPO) was added to the GB Mandatory Classification List (GB MCL) under the GB Classification, Labelling and Packaging (CLP) Regulation in February 2025. As per the requirements of Article 15 of the UK Cosmetic Regulation, Government is taking steps to prohibit the use of TPO in cosmetic products in Great Britain. Full details of the amendments to the Cosmetic Regulation, including any transitional provisions, will be prepared in due course. The first stage will be to ensure no new cosmetic products containing TPO are placed on the market from August 2026.”

‌



Changes on July 15, 2026

Two changes introduced by SI 2026/23 came into force in Great Britain on July 15.

These relate to:

the UV filter 4-MBC

warning labels on products containing formaldehyde-releasing preservatives

‌



The changes primarily affect cosmetic brands, manufacturers, importers and Responsible Persons, but salons should also be aware of them when purchasing and retailing products.

The UV filter 3-(4-methylbenzylidene)-camphor, commonly known as 4-MBC or Enzacamene, has been added to the list of substances prohibited in cosmetic products. The Government’s explanatory memorandum says the change follows scientific advice that there is “a potential risk to human health arising from the use of this substance in a cosmetic product”.

Changes on August 15

A second set of changes takes effect in Great Britain on August 15.

‌



These include:

a ban on 16 substances classified as carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic for reproduction, including TPO

new concentration limits for Hexyl Salicylate

For beauty professionals, TPO is likely to be the most relevant newly prohibited ingredient because it has been used in some UV- and LED-cured nail products.

Article continues below

TPO stands for Trimethylbenzoyl Diphenylphosphine Oxide. It acts as a photoinitiator in some UV- and LED-cured products, helping the formula harden when exposed to a curing lamp. The substances have been classified as category 1B or category 2 carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic for reproduction, commonly shortened to CMR substances.

News.title: What Harry and Meghan's 'half-in' royal life could look like as they 'eye up return'
News.content:
What Harry and Meghan's 'half-in' royal life could look like as they 'eye up return'

The Sussexes are reportedly hoping for a return to the royal fold - but will they be welcomed back? And what would the future look like for the pair?

View 8 Images After reuniting with the King this month, the Sussexes are hoping for a new 'deal' (Image: GETTY)

They've tried the American dream, but now Prince Harry and Meghan Markle seem to be turning back on their self-exile to the States.

‌



Seeing their children reunite with King Charles earlier this month was more than a precious family memory - sources close to Harry say it marked a huge step towards a new 'agreement' with the Firm. Pals have suggested that a return to the UK for the couple, in some form, is firmly on the agenda.

‌



Details of what happened during the meeting at Highgrove are scarce - the Sussexes are said to be under strict instruction to keep everything under wraps. But the brief family reunion has apparently buoyed Harry and Meghan into believing they can rekindle their relationship with the royal family - and reverse Megxit.

‌



Meghan Markle shares sweet holiday snaps of Archie and Lilibet visiting Diana's childhood home READ MORE :

Meghan Markle pictured on set of MasterChef as she signs up as celebrity judge READ MORE :

View 8 Images Meghan shared the holiday snaps with her 4.7million Instagram followers (Image: Meghan/Instagram)

In return for keeping things private, sources say that the Palace has accepted Harry can carry out charity events and public speaking engagements while in the UK as if he was still a 'working royal'. It's believed that there is a 'growing acceptance' from the Firm that the Sussexes will still need to continue their commercial ventures in order to fund their lifestyle and private security in sunny Montecito - marking a huge shift in understanding between both camps.

The couple have seen their popularity fade in the US, with lucrative deals with Spotify and Netflix drying up. Meghan, who has big plans to return to TV screens and expand her lifestyle brand into a global powerhouse, is said to be fully supportive of Harry's desire to reconnect with his roots.

‌



As royal historian Marlene Koenig tells the Mirror: "It is inevitable that Harry would want to spend more time in his homeland with his children. Meghan's perceptions of the UK have been diluted by the perceived behavior against her. But Harry wants his kids to connect with the UK and, perhaps, with family.

"The trust issue is serious. However, the fact that Charles and the Palace apparently took control of the Highgrove meeting – and there have been no leaks – is a sign that Charles wants to heal this relationship privately."

A 'half-in, half-out' scenario, where the couple would carry on making money in the US and elsewhere, while also carrying out royal engagements in the UK, is something the late Queen expressly forbade. But the couple are reportedly optimistic that if they can meet with the King on a more frequent basis, with their children, a similar deal could be on the table.

‌



So what could the Sussexes 'deal' actually look like? Let's take a closer look…

Where would they live?

Harry and Meghan were famously evicted from Frogmore Cottage after moving to the US on a permanent basis. Much like Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, they could benefit from being given a property on the King's private Norfolk estate. But given Harry's well-documented security concerns, setting up home here might be a stretch. Instead, it's been suggested that the couple will use their holiday home in Portugal as a base.

The Sussexes reportedly own a luxury property at the CostaTerra Golf and Ocean Club in Melides. They are believed to have bought the Portugal pad in 2023 for around £3.6million.

‌



8 View 8 Images The Sussexes enjoy a day at the beach (Image: Meghan/Instagram) 8 View 8 Images Meghan shared a snap of Portuguese fish restaurant, O Melidense, in Melidese (Image: Meghan/Instagram)

The exclusive oceanfront estate - often dubbed "the Hamptons of Portugal" - is located along the Alentejo coast, roughly 81 miles (130 kilometers) south of Lisbon. Neighbours include Princess Eugenie and her husband, Jack Brooksbank, who own a home in the same development. (Additionally, Jack works in the marketing and sales department for the resort.)

‌



This week, Meghan took to Instagram to share a selection of summer holiday snaps from Portugal, where the family had been enjoying a holiday before heading to the UK for the big reunion this month.

Certainly, Portugal currently seems the far more likely option - and not only because of Harry's security concerns. Marlene argues: "Meghan was not comfortable with all the rules. William was right to advise Harry to take his time and not rush into marriage. The family learned valuable lessons from the marital failures (Charles & Diana and Andrew & Sarah). Neither couple got to know each other well before the marriage. No real courtships.

"Edward and Sophie and William and Catherine lived together before their marriages. That time allowed the women to learn what life would be like as a royal. Meghan was not afforded that time – and perhaps if they lived together for a few years, Meghan would have had more time to observe."

‌



Kids' schooling

Recent reports have suggested that Harry would love for his two children Archie and Lilibet - now aged seven and five - to have a private British education, as he fears they are missing out on an "extensive family network".

8 View 8 Images Harry reportedly wants his children to receive a British education (Image: @meghan/Instagram) 8 View 8 Images Meghan shares a photo of Harry, Archie and Lilibet visiting Althorp (Image: Meghan/Instagram)

‌



His spokesperson did confirm earlier this year that son Archie would not be following in Harry's footsteps and going to Eton - unlike Prince George, who will start there in September. They said: "Prince Harry has not put his son's name down for Eton, nor does he have any plans to do so."

But there are plenty of other options available, including Marlborough College, Oundle School, and St Edward's School in Oxford - all of which were considerations for George.

Singer Joss Stone previously revealed that Harry had asked her about moving from America back to Britain during a conversation at the WellChild Awards in London on September 8. She told Hello!: "He also asked about how we were settling back in and was genuinely interested in our move home. He's just very warm and down to earth, as always.

‌



"Maybe Harry will move back too. That would be nice. He was saying how wonderful the schools are here and how important community is for children.

"It was nice to share that with him because it's exactly why we felt drawn to come back – for the kids to grow up surrounded by family, friends and a strong sense of belonging and most importantly in a safe environment."

It is possible that Archie could attend a boarding school, which would allow the Sussexes to continue to live in the US, or Portugal. But given Harry's own unhappy experience at Eton - which he went into detail about in Spare - boarding might be off the cards.

‌



What royal roles could they take on?

Harry and Meghan had to return their honorary military appointments and royal patronages after quitting royal life, and they were redistributed to working members of the Royal Family. Under the arrangement, the couple also had to give up using the HRH titles, but Harry retained the title of prince, having been born one.

It seems highly unlikely that Charles would take those redistributed patronages away from working royals in order to return them to Harry and Meghan. And they remain such polarising figures that putting them back into royal circulation might be too much of a risk.

But it appears that the Sussexes are hoping that Harry could carry out public-facing events while in the UK - like hospital visits and speeches - as a working royal would.

‌



View 8 Images Harry and Meghan on a trip to Australia earlier this year (Image: Getty Images)

Could Harry and Meghan's 'half-in' format really come to fruition? Certainly the Sussexes are a polarising couple, and there isn't a huge feeling of goodwill towards them given their comments on the royal family in the Queen and Prince Philip's latter years. Reinstating them on any level will likely prove contentious.

Then there is the William factor. He will one day become King and has made no secret of his desire to slim down the monarchy and make changes. Certainly it seems there will be no place for Harry or Meghan.

‌



William is known to take a much harder line than Charles, and while he was said to be supportive of his father's decision to see the Sussexes this month, his stance on them has not changed. Sources say neither he nor Princess Kate had any desire to meet with Harry and Meghan - and the once close bond the brothers shared looks irreparably shattered.

Private ventures

Harry currently earns money from business coaching company BetterUp and sustainable travel firm Travalyst, and is also trying to expand the success of the couple's production company Archewell.

Meghan, meanwhile, runs her own lucrative lifestyle business, As Ever, with a return to acting in the works as well as other TV appearances - including being a guest judge recently on MasterChef Australia.

‌



But what hurdles could they face pairing their commercial work with royal duties? Marlene explains: "The Sussexes did not want the half-in-half -out guidelines that were offered by the Palace [before Megxit] – which were the Luce Guidelines designed for Edward and Sophie, who were half in, half out for a period of time before Ardent [the television production company founded by Prince Edward in 1993] had financial problems and Sophie's encounter with the fake sheik.

View 8 Images Meghan as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia

"On the premise that the Queen needed more support during the Golden Jubilee, Edward and Sophie gave up their careers, closed down their businesses, and became very successful working royals. The Luce guidelines had restrictions. Everything would need to be approved by the Palace – the business deals. Let's be honest, the Palace would never have approved the Netflix deal."

‌



The key rules of the Luce Guidelines dictate that working royals must consult the Lord Chamberlain prior to taking on any new business, commercial, or professional activities.

Business ventures must be strictly separated from official royal duties and public engagements; royals must turn down official public engagements if they cannot adequately separate them from their private business interests.

Commercial enterprises involving royals must also ensure that employees or associates do not exploit royal connections or status for financial advantage. Finally, working royals are barred from using their official titles, residences, or royal patronage to promote private commercial interests.

‌



Security

Harry has argued for years that his family are not safe in the UK unless he is afforded taxpayer funded police protection. It is equivalent to the automatic high-level security provided to full-time senior working royals like Prince William and Princess Kate.

He lost an appeal over the dismissal of his High Court claim against the Home Office last year after RAVEC decided he should receive a reduced degree of security protection when in the country.

Harry tried to have his security upgraded ahead of July's visit; a report was submitted - commissioned by Harry's own private security firm - detailing dozens of threats and potential attacks. But he was again told that no taxpayer funded security would be provided.

Article continues below

If the Sussexes stay at a royal residence during their trips to the UK, they gain the security protections that come with it. But outside of those walls, it's a different picture.

King Charles cannot change or unilaterally restore Harry's official taxpayer-funded police security. As a constitutional monarch, the King must remain strictly apolitical and cannot interfere in government decisions or ongoing legal proceedings. He therefore cannot interfere with Ravec's decision making.

News.title: UK weather maps show 40C heatwave within days as 18 counties hit 39C or more
News.content:
UK weather maps show 40C heatwave within days as 18 counties hit 39C or more

Weather forecasting models show temperatures surging as high as 40C in England next week, with the Met Office warning of another potential heatwave to come

View 5 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures soaring well above the average in England and Wales next week (Image: WXCHARTS)

The Met Office says some parts of the UK may see the fourth heatwave of the year next week - and now weather models suggest temperatures could surge to a staggering 40C.

‌



The GFS weather model first shows temperatures rising on Tuesday, hitting 33C in eastern and southern England, while 31C highs are possible as far north as Yorkshire.

‌



Conditions are expected to turn even warmer on Wednesday, with the data showing potential highs of 35C in the south-east. The Midlands could reach 33C, with 32C coming along the England-Wales border. Temperatures in Scotland and Northern Ireland are expected to be significantly cooler, struggling to rise past the low-20s.

‌



View 5 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Thursday (Image: WXCHARTS)

UK weather maps show heatwave reaching 37C in seven counties within six days READ MORE :

UK weather maps show 39C heatwave and hottest day of year as 10 counties hit 38C READ MORE :

Extremely hot conditions are possible on Thursday. The GFS model shows sweltering 39C highs in central, southern and south-eastern England quite widely. This would smash the current temperature record for 2026, which is 37.7C (set on June 26 in Lingwood, Norfolk).

Highs of 37C are possible on Friday in eastern areas, the maps suggest, with 35-36C on the cards across most of central and southern England. While Saturday could bring a return of 38C-39C temperatures - when eastern England is expected to be the warmest region.

‌



View 5 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Friday (Image: WXCHARTS)

This heatwave should peak on Sunday with highs of 40C possible, once again in eastern England. Such temperatures would mean we may potentially see a new all-time temperature record for the UK. The current record stands at 40.3C, which came during the infamous July 2022 heatwave.

Temperature anomaly maps for next week show England and Wales shaded in areas of dark red and black. This indicates where temperatures are expected to rise well above the seasonal average.

‌



View 5 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) at 6pm on Saturday (Image: WXCHARTS)

GFS model data suggests as many as 18 counties may see temperatures rise to 39C or more next week. They are all in England.

“[There is] the possibility that some locations may once again reach heatwave criteria, potentially making this the fourth heatwave episode of the year for parts of the UK,” the Met Office says.

News.title: Food waste bin rules explained - including surprising free item you can use as a liner
News.content:
Food waste bin rules explained - including surprising free item you can use as a liner

Buying liners for food waste bins can add up but there is a little-known alternative that could save money

View 2 Images The caddies have been introduced the UK

People have been reminded what they can often put in a food waste bin - and it might include one surprising item. Under rules which came into force this year councils must provide separate food waste collections for every household.

However while some local authorities provide free replacement biodegradable bags to line the bins others say residents must provide their own after using up the first roll. This can cost around £1.80 for 20 leaving some people unhappy at the additional cost.

But one council has taken to Facebook to share a little-known fact about what you can use to line your food caddy - and it might just be not only money-saving but can reduce your other waste. In a video Darlington Council explained its rules telling its residents: "Did you know you can use any plastic bag, bin liner or even newspaper to line your food caddy?"

While people must check their own local authority as each can be different, many others do use similar sorting methods to Darlington which means they can also use unwanted plastic bags and even empty bread bags. These include Scottish Borders Council, Devon County Council, City of Lincoln Council and Sandwell Council.

City of Lincoln Council explained how the system works. It said: "At the processing plant, the first step is to remove the bags using a specialised machine, allowing you to use any bag as a liner.

"After they have been removed at the anaerobic digestion plant, the bags are sent to the Energy from Waste facility, where they’re used to generate energy. They would normally go there anyway in your black bin, but this way they’ve had a second life as a food waste liner first.

"Using a liner helps keep your caddy clean and makes it easier to empty, so a great option is to reuse plastic bags you already have at home." It suggested using:

Bread bags

Frozen food bags

Online shopping packaging

Other small plastic bags from everyday items

The council added: "Once you start saving them, you might be surprised how many you still come across! There is also the option to line your caddy with newspaper or use no liner at all."

It added: "If this is your preference, you may need to wash your caddy more regularly. With food waste no longer going in your normal kitchen bin, you might also find you use fewer bin liners overall."

And Devon County Council said: "If you have a waste caddy, remember you can reuse any bag as a liner. Food waste collections are in place across most of Devon, and they are easier to use than ever.

"And those households with a food waste caddy don’t need to buy special compostable bags, they can just reuse any plastic or paper bag they’ve already got, such as an empty bread bag, salad bag, cereal bag or frozen vegetable bag."

Environment boost

It said that despite the changes, food waste was still a big problem in Devon, with almost a third of waste in general household bins being made up of food. A study found that four-fifths (79%) of the food waste in Devon’s black bins could have been avoided, and a third (35%) was still in its packaging.

It explained how recycling food waste and plastic bags can help in several ways. It said: "All liners/bags are removed at the processing facility before the food waste is treated.

"They are then sent to an Energy from Waste facility where they are converted into energy. The food waste is processed to produce energy and a liquid fertiliser."

View 2 Images Most households now have several bins

However other local authorities, including Durham County Council, Stockport Council and Rochdale Council, have strict rules around only using biodegradable bags as they use a different processing method. Stockport Council said: "Do not use biodegradable plastic bags from supermarkets as they break down into little bits of plastic and are not compostable."

What else can go in a food waste bin?

While again, individual councils can have different rules, so people must check with their local authority, most are similar. Redcar and Cleveland Council said: "You can include all food waste from your home, including leftovers from meals, food that has gone past its use-by date, and any other food waste from your kitchen."

It listed the allowed items as:

fruit - raw and cooked

salad and vegetables - raw and cooked

vegetable and fruit peelings - including banana skins, cherry stones etc

tea bags (including the bag) and coffee grounds

bread, cakes and other baked goods

pasta, rice, beans and pulses

meat - raw and cooked, bones

fish/shellfish - raw and cooked, including bones and shells

eggs and egg products (including eggshells)

dairy products (including cheese and yogurts)

tinned and dry pet food

small amounts of gravy, sauces or custard left on food

any meal or take-away leftovers
