World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Why public servants have less than a month to update pension records
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Public servants given until August 14 to update pension records [File]

Government has directed all public servants to update their records with the Public Service Superannuation Fund (PSSF) by August 14, 2026, in the latest step towards modernising pension administration.

In a circular signed by Principal Secretary for Public Service and Human Capital Development Dr Jane Imbunya, all PSSF members are expected to update their personal information and beneficiary details through the PSSF Member Self-Service Portal or the PSSF Mobile Application.

The circular was addressed to Ministries, State Departments, Constitutional Commissions, Independent Offices, County Public Service Boards and County Governments.

The exercise is expected to streamline pension administration and accelerate the processing of retirement benefits supported by a new Pension Administration System (PAS), a digital platform developed by PSSF to deliver faster, more transparent and more efficient pension services.

The registration exercise targets 529,635 members drawn from across the public service, including 332,950 teachers under the Teachers Service Commission (TSC), 120,084 officers in the disciplined services, 60,322 employees in Ministries, Departments, Constitutional Commissions and Agencies (MDCAs), and 16,279 county government employees.

PSSF Chief Executive Jonah Aiyabei said updating member records is critical to the success of the pension reforms and the delivery of efficient retirement services.

“By updating their records, public servants will enable quicker processing of retirement benefits, reduce administrative delays, improve data integrity, allow members to access pension services seamlessly through digital channels and ensure that the right benefits reach the right beneficiaries at the right time,” he said.

Under the new system, members can access their pension statements in real time, monitor contributions, view projected retirement benefits, update beneficiary nominations and personal details and initiate and track pension claims remotely.

The platform also features a Sponsor Portal that enables employer institutions to submit payroll information, contribution schedules and member data electronically, significantly improving efficiency and accountability in pension administration.

Dr Aiyabei said the Pension Administration System marks a significant milestone in the government’s efforts to digitise pension administration and restore dignity to retirees through faster, more accessible and transparent services.

“It will provide our members with real-time access to their pension information, enable seamless engagement with the Fund and support a fully digital, paperless pension administration process. Ultimately, our goal is to restore dignity in old age by ensuring every public servant receives timely and efficient pension services,” he said.

World.title: Inside Kenya's Ebola defences as seven Americans enter quarantine
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

A doctor provides care to a patient with Ebola virus disease at the Rwampara Ebola Treatment Centre (ETC) in Bunia, Ituri, July 13, 2026. [AFP]

Seven American humanitarian workers are spending 21 days under medical observation in Kenya not because they are ill, but because they could become ill.

A Reuters report published today confirms they are seven American Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) staff from the Christian humanitarian organisation Samaritan's Purse . Franklin Graham, the organisation's President and CEO, confirmed this, saying:

“Samaritan's Purse has seven American Disaster Assistance Response Team staff members there. None of them have any symptoms, but they are being quarantined by the Kenyan government for 21 days."

The aid workers, all returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where they were involved in responding to the world's largest recorded outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, have no symptoms and have not tested positive for the virus.

Yet under new US public health rules, they cannot travel home immediately. Instead, they are completing a precautionary quarantine on Kenyan soil.

Their arrival has reignited debate over Kenya's role in regional outbreak preparedness and raised a question that extends far beyond the fate of the seven Americans:

If Ebola crossed Kenya's borders tomorrow, is the country ready?

The answer, infectious disease experts say, lies not in panic but in years of quiet preparation that most Kenyans have never seen.

That preparedness became evident during a recent visit by The Standard to Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH), where access to one of the hospital's high-security isolation areas was restricted.

Hospital officials informed the reporting team that patients with Mpox were being managed in the unit and, for safety reasons, journalists were not allowed to enter or film inside.

The brief encounter offered a glimpse into the strict infection prevention measures that underpin Kenya's readiness for dangerous infectious diseases.

According to an infectious disease physician at the Kenyatta National Hospital and head of the isolation ward, preparedness is far more than having an isolation room.

"One thing we should never do as Kenyans is panic," he says. "Panic only makes the situation worse. Instead, we should ask ourselves one question: Are we prepared?"

His answer is unequivocal. "As a government and as health institutions, we are in preparedness mode."

Dr Nyukuri explains that preparedness begins long before the first patient arrives at a hospital.

It means evaluating whether enough trained personnel are available, whether laboratories have the necessary testing reagents, whether protective equipment is adequate, and whether health workers understand every step required to safely manage a suspected Ebola patient.

"Here at Kenyatta National Hospital, we have conducted extensive training for healthcare workers," he says. "We have carried out readiness assessments, simulated patient scenarios and practised every stage of care from the moment a suspected patient arrives, through admission, isolation and treatment."

The simulations, he explains, are designed to ensure that no decision is being made for the first time during a real emergency. "When we eventually encounter a suspected case, it should not be something new to us." Dr Duncan Nyukuri, an Infectious Diseases specialist, during an interview with The Standard on July 16, 2026 at Kenyatta National Hospital. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

Preparedness also extends beyond hospitals. Health surveillance teams remain stationed at airports and land border crossings, screening travellers arriving from affected regions while rapid response teams stand ready to investigate suspected infections.

"So far, Kenya has done a good job," Dr Nyukuri says. "We have not recorded a confirmed case despite the increasing numbers in the DRC. We pray that remains the case. But if we receive one patient, we are prepared."

How Ebola jumps from animals to people

Although Ebola is often associated with outbreaks, the virus begins its journey quietly in nature.

Dr Nyukuri explains that fruit bats are believed to be the natural reservoir of the virus. "They carry the virus without becoming sick themselves," he says.

Problems arise when increasing human activity brings people into closer contact with wildlife.

Mining, logging, hunting, charcoal burning, expanding settlements and encroachment into forests all increase the likelihood of viruses crossing from animals into humans.

"We call these zoonotic diseases," Dr Nyukuri explains. "Once the virus infects a human being, it can then spread from person to person through contact with infected body fluids, leading to outbreaks within families and communities."

You see, Ebola is a family; many people speak about Ebola as though it were a single virus.

In reality, scientists recognise five different species.

The best known is the Zaire strain, responsible for the devastating West African epidemic between 2014 and 2016.

"It is highly infectious and highly deadly," says Dr Nyukuri. "But because we have studied it extensively, we now have licensed vaccines and effective treatment options."

The Sudan strain, which has repeatedly caused outbreaks in Uganda, is the second most significant.

The current emergency, however, involves the Bundibugyo strain, first identified in Uganda's Bundibugyo District.

"This is the third recorded outbreak caused by Bundibugyo," Dr Nyukuri explains. "We have not studied it nearly as much as the Zaire strain."

There is currently no licensed vaccine specifically targeting Bundibugyo Ebola.

Instead, researchers are evaluating experimental vaccines while clinical trials in eastern DRC are testing promising treatments, including the monoclonal antibody MBP134 and the antiviral drug remdesivir.

"That is why this outbreak concerns many of us," he says. "We still have limited tools compared to what exists for the Zaire strain."

While Kenya has not recorded a confirmed case linked to the current outbreak, neighbouring countries remain on high alert.

Uganda on Thursday declared its last Ebola patient and has begun the mandatory 42-day countdown required before the country can officially be declared Ebola-free.

In contrast, eastern DRC continues battling sustained transmission, placing enormous pressure on treatment centres and frontline health workers.

It is against that backdrop that Kenya has found itself playing an increasingly important role in regional preparedness.

Their presence has nevertheless fuelled public debate over Kenya's preparedness infrastructure and the country's place in global health security.

Earlier this week, two American humanitarian workers who contracted Ebola while working in eastern DRC were medically evacuated to Germany for specialised treatment after receiving initial care in Bunia. Their evacuation underscores an important distinction: Kenya is currently serving as a precautionary observation site for exposed but healthy personnel, while confirmed Ebola patients requiring advanced clinical care have been transferred to Germany.

For Dr Nyukuri, the conversation should remain grounded in science rather than fear.

Preparedness, he says, is not measured only by isolation wards or specialised equipment, but by the ability of an entire health system to detect threats early, respond quickly and protect both patients and healthcare workers.

"My prayer is that Kenya never records a case," he says. "But preparedness means planning for the day you hope never comes."

As seven healthy humanitarian workers quietly complete their quarantine in Kenya, that preparation is no longer an abstract exercise.

It is being tested in real time. The development has also drawn attention to the contrasting roles played by East African countries during the current outbreak.

Uganda, widely regarded as one of Africa's most experienced countries in responding to Ebola, recently brought its own outbreak under control and has now entered the 42-day countdown required to be declared Ebola-free. Over the years, the country has built a reputation for rapidly detecting cases, tracing contacts and isolating patients, earning praise from the World Health Organization for repeatedly containing outbreaks before they spread widely.

Yet despite that experience, Uganda did not become a destination for foreign humanitarian workers requiring precautionary quarantine or post-exposure observation.

Instead, that role has fallen to Kenya, where seven American aid workers are now completing a mandatory 21-day quarantine after working in Ebola-affected areas of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The contrast raises broader questions about how countries are selected to support international outbreak responses. While Uganda has demonstrated its capacity to treat Ebola patients within its own borders, Kenya's involvement appears to reflect a different function—serving as a precautionary observation site for exposed personnel rather than a treatment centre for confirmed cases.

Health experts caution against interpreting the distinction as a measure of either country's clinical capability. Instead, they say such decisions are often influenced by a combination of bilateral agreements, operational logistics, evacuation arrangements and the specific objectives of international public health partners.

World.title: MPs push for urgent resolution of higher education funding crisis
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

HELB Chief Executive Officer Geoffrey Monari before the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Education on July 16, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

The National Assembly Departmental Committee on Education has called for urgent and coordinated action to address persistent funding challenges affecting Kenya's higher education sector.

The MPs proposed a joint engagement involving Parliament, the National Treasury and the Ministry of Education to streamline implementation of the Higher Education Funding Model.

The committee, chaired by Vice Chairperson Eve Obara, made the recommendation after holding separate meetings with officials from the State Department for Higher Education, the Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) and the Universities Fund during a review of the 2025/2026 Budget Implementation Status.

Appearing before the committee, Higher Education Principal Secretary Dr. Beatrice Inyangala said the Higher Education Funding Model is operational but continues to face implementation challenges due to inadequate alignment between the funding framework and budget allocations.

"The funding model is functional. However, the main challenge lies in budget alignment," Dr. Inyangala told Members.

The funding model was introduced to allocate financial support to university students based on their level of need, while ensuring sustainable financing for public universities.

However, implementation has generated debate over affordability, funding adequacy and delays in disbursement of resources to institutions.

MPs observed that the mismatch between policy and budgetary allocations has undermined effective financing of universities and agreed that a joint meeting involving the National Treasury, the Ministry of Education and Parliament would help harmonise the funding framework.

The committee also sought explanations over the growing stock of pending bills owed by public universities.

Dr. Inyangala informed Members that most of the outstanding obligations were inherited over several years, with universities continuing efforts to clear the debts despite increasing interest charges.

According to the State Department for Higher Education, public universities had accumulated pending bills amounting to Sh100.3 billion as of January 2026.

The ministry said institutions are prioritising settlement of pending obligations, suspending stalled development projects and exploring alternative revenue streams to prevent further accumulation of debt.

During a separate session, Members questioned HELB officials on how the board allocates student loans when available funding cannot meet demand from all eligible applicants.

Led by Chief Executive Officer Geoffrey Monari, HELB officials were asked to explain the criteria used in determining beneficiaries during periods of constrained resources.

Legislators emphasised that the allocation process should be fair, transparent and predictable to protect deserving students from being unfairly excluded.

World.title: Hamza Abdelkarim set for senior Barcelona debut in pre-season friendly vs. CE Europa
World.content:
Hamza Abdelkarim, the Barcelona star, is preparing to play his first match with the first team during the pre-season preparation camp.

Abdelkarim is currently training with Barcelona under German manager Hansi Flick in the team’s pre-season camp. Barcelona is scheduled to play its first friendly match of the camp on Friday at the sports complex against CE Europa.

Today’s match will offer Abdelkarim a valuable opportunity to showcase his talents and impress the manager, provided Flick gives him the chance to feature on the pitch.

Abdelkarim came through the youth academy of Egyptian giants Al Ahly. In January 2026, he moved to Barcelona Atlètic (FC Barcelona B) on a six-month loan deal. Following impressive performances, Barcelona secured his transfer on a permanent contract running through June 2029.

Before entering Al Ahly’s academy, he took his first steps in youth football in Malaysia, spending 2016 to 2020 with FC Kuala Lumpur and Little League Soccer while residing there as a youngster.

World.title: EgyptAir honors doctor who saved passenger’s life mid-flight from London
World.content:
Pilot Ahmed Adel, Chairman and Executive Managing Director of EgyptAir Holding Company, honored Dr. Marwa Salah for her humanitarian efforts and professional medical intervention in saving a passenger’s life.

The passenger suffered a sudden health emergency aboard EgyptAir Flight MS780 traveling from London Heathrow to Cairo International Airport on July 10, 2026.

The chairman expressed his appreciation to Dr. Salah, noting that her actions reflected the highest values of humanity and professional duty. He awarded her a complimentary EgyptAir ticket.

Additionally, he honored the cabin crew for their efficient, professional handling of the emergency, which helped ensure the passenger’s safety until the flight landed safely.

In a statement shared following the incident, the passenger noted that Dr. Salah stayed by his side for over two hours, providing critical medical care under highly challenging conditions with support from other doctors on board, the cabin crew, and the flight captain.

The passenger also praised EgyptAir’s rapid response, as the airline arranged for an ambulance and a medical team to meet the aircraft immediately upon arrival in Cairo, enabling him to receive prompt follow-up care and stabilize his condition.

World.title: “It’s time to do in the West Bank what we did in Gaza”: Israeli National Security Minister
World.content:
Reactions flooded in from Israeli officials following the death of an Israeli and the injury of others during clashes that erupted after settlers stormed the village of Till in the occupied West Bank—events that also led to the martyrdom of four Palestinians.

The incidents occurred near the village of Till and the Havat Gilad settlement outpost. The Palestinian town was subjected to attacks by settlers, sparking hand-to-hand clashes as Palestinians attempted to defend their homes and land from ongoing assaults carried out under the cover of the Israeli army.

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that he would hold an urgent meeting shortly with Defense Minister Israel Katz and IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir to discuss responses to the events in Till, near Nablus, which took place this morning near Havat Gilad.

On his X account, Netanyahu stated: “We will act with full force against the perpetrators of the attack and those behind them, and we will not allow terrorism to raise its head again in Judea and Samaria [the Israeli term for the West Bank].”

Demands for harsher measures and replicating the Gaza model

Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir—speaking on his way to join Netanyahu at a Cabinet meeting—called for cities and villages in the occupied West Bank to meet a fate similar to that of Beit Hanoun in Gaza, which was destroyed by the Israeli army.

Ben-Gvir indicated he would demand orders for the military to flatten the homes of attackers and their supporters using airstrikes and D9 bulldozers, claiming this would exact the price Palestinians deserve.

He added: “For every Jew killed, the enemy must lose land and homes. This is the language understood in the Middle East, and just as we spoke it in Gaza, it is time to speak it in Judea and Samaria as well.”

Similarly, Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich commented on the incident, stating: “The erosion of deterrence and the increasing boldness of our enemies in recent weeks against settlement pioneers and outpost residents cannot be accepted as normal.”

He continued: “I demand that the IDF act decisively against the village from which the attackers emerged and the surrounding areas, to restore control and re-establish deterrence.”

Military decisions to reinforce troops

According to the Hebrew newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth, IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir conducted a situational assessment following the incident in Till. The Israeli military stated that, as part of this assessment, the Chief of Staff ordered a wide-scale reinforcement of forces to bolster defensive measures in the area and capture all the gunmen involved in the attack.

World.title: Egypt bans poisoning of street dogs under new national strategy
World.content:
Egypt’s Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation has launched a unified national strategy to manage the country’s street animal population. The initiative establishes scientific and veterinary standards across state institutions to handle stray animals safely.

Key details of the new national plan include:

1. Restructuring veterinary policies

Following directives from President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, a committee comprising representatives from relevant ministries and state authorities has been formed to overhaul veterinary policies and unify management efforts.

2. Adoption of the TNR Program

The strategy relies on the Trap-Neuter-Vaccinate-Return (TNR) framework. Street dogs will be vaccinated against rabies, spayed or neutered, and returned to their habitats, mirroring internationally recognized protocols for managing stray populations.

3. Ban on culling and poisoning

The ministry ordered an immediate halt to indiscriminate control methods. The plan strictly prohibits mass culling, the use of poison, and unauthorized animal relocations. Legal action will be taken against violators.

4. Alignment with international standards

The ministry emphasized that the plan aligns with Egypt’s commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity and complies with guidelines set by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH).

5. Strict oversight and measures against misinformation

All citizens, institutions, civil society organizations, and local authorities are instructed to adhere strictly to the new protocol. Unilateral decisions outside the approved framework are prohibited. The ministry warned that strict legal action, coordinated with security and regulatory bodies, will be taken against unauthorized practices or deliberate attempts to mislead the public.

6. Modernizing veterinary infrastructure

The initiative includes upgrading veterinary units, slaughterhouses, and diagnostic laboratories. It also calls for legislative updates, digital transformation, and the creation of smart database platforms for crisis management.

7. Ecological balance and public health

The plan aims to strike a balance between safeguarding public health and preserving ecological integrity through sustained vaccination drives, neutering programs, and science-backed management.

World.title: Marriott signs LE56 billion deal in Egypt with major 9-hotel expansion
World.content:
Marriott International has signed a deal with Misr Italia Properties and People & Places Real Estate Development to build nine new hotels and resorts across Egypt, adding over 1,800 rooms and suites to the country’s coastal and urban destinations, Masrawy reported.

The agreement covers five mixed-use developments containing 11 hotels, branded residential units, and a standalone hotel.

The deal was signed by Shady Hassan, Marriott’s Vice President of Development for North Africa, alongside Misr Italia Properties co-CEOs and People & Places co-founders Mohamed Khaled El Assal and Karim Khaled El Assal.

Tourism Minister Sherif Fathy noted that expanding hotel capacity aligns with state efforts to boost tourism infrastructure and meet projected growth in incoming international visitors.

According to Mohamed Khaled El Assal, Misr Italia is committing over LE 56.7 billion to hospitality expansion. The projects are projected to generate around 6,000 direct and indirect jobs and accommodate up to 373,000 tourists annually.

Karim Khaled El Assal added that the combined efforts between the companies have so far developed a portfolio of more than 1,800 hotel rooms and branded residences across key regions in the country.

World.title: 4 Palestinians and 1 Israeli killed in West Bank clashes near Nablus
World.content:
The town of Till, located southwest of Nablus near the Havat Gilad settlement outpost in the occupied West Bank, witnessed a surge of Israeli aggression.

The Israeli escalation resulted in the killing of four Palestinians and the injury of four others, alongside the death of one Israeli and the injury of two others, whose conditions range from serious to critical.

Details of the clashes and shooting incident

Events unfolded after Israeli settlers stormed and attacked the town of Till. Violent hand-to-hand clashes erupted between local residents and settlers near a mosque as Palestinians attempted to defend their homes and lands against attacks carried out under the protection of the Israeli army.

According to Israeli accounts and settlers—as reported by Israel Hayom and Yedioth Ahronoth—upon the arrival of a security guard from the Gilad farm at the scene, a Palestinian citizen managed to seize the officer’s weapon and open fire on Israelis present, causing casualties before the weapon was subsequently recovered.

According to statements from the Palestinian Ministry of Health, Israeli military fire in the town of Till resulted in the killing of four Palestinians and injured four others, with three of the wounded reported to be in serious or critical condition.

On the Israeli side, medical crews and Israeli sources announced the death of a man in his 30s following prolonged resuscitation attempts at the scene due to gunshot wounds to his body.

The Magen David Adom emergency service confirmed that significant forces and an armored ambulance were dispatched to the site, where first aid was rendered to a 25-year-old man suffering from a gunshot wound to his upper body; he remained fully conscious and was evacuated via military helicopter. Ichilov Hospital confirmed receiving two injured individuals evacuated by air—one in critical condition around 20 years old, and a 25-year-old in serious condition whose status later stabilized.

Escalation measures and military siege

Al Jazeera’s correspondent and the Israeli military spokesperson reported that Israeli forces imposed a complete military siege and blockade on the city of Nablus and the town of Till, sealing main entrances and deploying additional military reinforcements to the perimeter surrounding the Gilad farm.

According to media reports, settlers opened fire on Palestinians in the town following the attack, coinciding with Israeli soldiers firing tear gas at local residents in the area.

Escalating context in the region

These developments mark the third such incident in the region within 24 hours. Just yesterday, Itamar Cohen, one of the founders of agricultural outposts in the West Bank, was stabbed near the Elon Moreh settlement, while another individual was injured in a separate stabbing incident in the northern occupied West Bank, after which the assailant was shot dead by Israeli forces.

World.title: “Not a single drop of oil”: Iran issues stark warning to US over infrastructure threats
World.content:
The Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters stated in a press release on Wednesday, that US President Donald Trump has resumed threatening Iran with strikes on its infrastructure.

“The Strait of Hormuz remains closed, and if any vessel is permitted passage, it will proceed solely along the designated route and under the previously announced protocols,” the headquarters’ leadership said in the statement.

The statement added that if the United States carries out its threats, the Iranian Armed Forces will not allow “even a single drop of oil to be exported,” warning that oil, gas, electricity, and economic infrastructure throughout the region will become targets for attacks.

It further stressed that repeated threats from the US and its military will only broaden the scope of the war across the region, and potentially beyond.

Trump had previously declared that “if Iran fires a missile, shell, drone, or any other weapon at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz at any time, the United States will bomb and destroy a bridge or power station—including those located in or near the capital, Tehran.

World.title: Reviving a legend: Farrah El Dibany to star in new musical bringing Dalida’s life story to the stage
World.content:
A new Egyptian-French musical play commemorating the 40th anniversary of the legendary singer Dalida’s passing, was officially announced during a press conference at the residence of the French Ambassador in Cairo. The launch featured French Ambassador Éric Chevallier, Egyptian mezzo-soprano Farrah El Dibany, film director Khairy Beshara, and writer Waleed Khairy.

The project is an Egyptian-French collaboration staged as part of the “Mediterranean Season 2026,” an initiative aimed at fostering cultural and artistic exchange among regional nations while highlighting the shared creativity and cultural diversity of Mediterranean peoples.

Scheduled to serve as the grand finale of the season, the production will premiere at the Bibliotheca Alexandrina on October 31, followed by performances in Cairo in November.

During the press conference, French Ambassador Éric Chevallier underscored the vital significance of Egyptian-French cultural cooperation, noting that the production represents a major step in reviving Dalida’s legacy through a joint musical theater venture.

For her part, Farrah El Dibany shared that portraying Dalida had been a childhood dream. She explained that she pitched the concept to director Khairy Beshara, who collaborated with writer Waleed Khairy to develop the idea into a full-fledged theatrical project.

Beshara stated that the work aims to present different facets of Dalida’s personality beyond her familiar stage persona, while writer Waleed Khairy explained that his script focuses on humanizing the artist by highlighting lesser-known aspects of her life. The production is produced by Ahmed Fawzi.

The play chronicles Dalida’s artistic and personal journey, emphasizing her deep connection to Egypt and the profound impact of her Egyptian upbringing on her artistic identity. It also features a fresh musical vision arranged by French-Armenian composer André Manoukian.

The show falls under the umbrella of the “Mediterranean Season 2026,” an initiative launched in 2023 by French President Emmanuel Macron and organized with the support of the French Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Culture.

Running from May 15 to October 31, 2026, across France and several Mediterranean nations—including Egypt, Lebanon, Tunisia, Algeria, and Morocco—the initiative seeks to strengthen cultural ties and support creative endeavors throughout the region.

World.title: OPINION: Nyon’go, Nyon’go Nyon’go: Has the ‘Mufasa Effect’ of the Two Boys Gotten Under HH’s Skin?
World.content:
Nyon’go, Nyon’go: Has the ‘Mufasa Effect’ of the Two Boys Gotten Under HH’s Skin?

By Mabvuto Banda

There are moments in an election campaign when a politician says far more through his temperament than through the actual words coming out of his mouth. President Hakainde Hichilema’s repeated “Nyon’go, Nyon’go, Nyon’go” utterances, directed at Gary Nkombo, may have been intended as political theatre, but they revealed something else: a President appearing increasingly willing to abandon presidential restraint and descend into the language of irritation and ridicule. The “Nyon’go” remarks were not directed at Brian Mundubile or Makebi Zulu, and that distinction matters. But so does the temperament behind them. At this stage of an increasingly competitive campaign, such an outburst inevitably raises questions about whether the pressure is beginning to show.

For a man who is not only Head of State but also an elder in the church, the tone was particularly striking. A President is entitled to campaign aggressively, defend his record and challenge his opponents, but there is a difference between campaigning hard and appearing to lose the dignity that comes with the office. The presidency does not disappear simply because there is a microphone, a rally and an opponent to attack. And perhaps that is where the real story lies. Something appears to be getting under the President’s skin.

The “Nyon’go” episode may have involved Nkombo, but elsewhere on the campaign trail, the two men Hichilema repeatedly dismisses as “boys” have brought something to this election that also seems to be testing his patience. The confidence remains, but increasingly, so does the irritation.

THE MUFASA EFFECT

It is becoming something of a Mufasa effect. In The Lion King, Mufasa’s name alone carried weight. Mention it in the wrong company and the reaction was immediate: fear, discomfort and a sudden change of mood. Mufasa did not even have to enter the room. Sometimes the name alone was enough.

That is increasingly what Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu appear to be doing to President Hichilema politically. These are the same two men he has repeatedly reduced to “boys”, yet listen to how much political attention they now command. The more dismissive the language becomes, the harder it is to believe that the people being dismissed are politically irrelevant. If the “boys” do not matter, why do they appear to provoke such a reaction?

That is the Mufasa effect. It is not necessarily about who is stronger or who will ultimately win on August 13. That decision belongs to the Zambian people. It is about the psychological effect an opponent begins to have on another. Right now, Mundubile and Zulu appear to have found a way of occupying political space that their supposed insignificance should never have allowed.

THEN CAME THE COPPERBELT

Then came the Copperbelt, where NRPUP campaign vehicles were reportedly attacked and their windows shattered by people the opposition identified as UPND cadres. A driver was allegedly assaulted, while cash and a mobile phone were reportedly stolen from the convoy. Later came the extraordinary scenes in Luanshya, where Mundubile’s convoy encountered a police blockade as it attempted to reach supporters waiting in Mpatamatu.

And that begs an even bigger question: what peace is President Hakainde Hichilema actually talking about? On the ground in Mpatamatu on Friday, peace looked like this: an opposition convoy pelted with stones, a road into Luanshya sealed off by the very police force that is supposed to protect every candidate equally, and a presidential hopeful forced to talk his way past a blockade simply to reach voters who had been waiting for him.

If this is what the President’s “peace” produces, it is worth asking who it is actually peaceful for, because it was certainly not peaceful for Mundubile’s campaign. Vehicles were stoned. Police blocked the road. And this was not an isolated incident. On the same day, NRPUP campaign vehicles elsewhere on the Copperbelt reportedly had their windows smashed, a driver assaulted, and cash and a phone stolen.

Mundubile said his people had been attacked, assaulted and their vehicles vandalised while the government continued to speak of a peaceful campaign season. That description of peace is becoming increasingly difficult to reconcile with what Zambians are seeing.

KALINGALINGA CANNOT BE ERASED

And Luanshya did not happen in a vacuum. Only a week earlier came Kalingalinga, where police used teargas during a confrontation surrounding an opposition campaign event and reports emerged that a young girl had been shot. Government officials subsequently disputed aspects of the account, maintaining that police had used teargas and that no lives were lost. Whatever version one accepts, Kalingalinga raised uncomfortable questions about the policing of opposition political activities during an already heated election campaign.

Then, on the same afternoon as the Luanshya blockade, police walked onto Mundubile’s campaign stage in Ndola. By the time his convoy encountered trouble in Luanshya, interaction with law enforcement was becoming part of the opposition’s campaign story rather than something happening at its margins. Kalingalinga, Ndola and Luanshya have different circumstances and must each be judged on their own facts, but taken together with the reported attacks on campaign vehicles, they leave an uncomfortable question about the environment in which the opposition is being expected to campaign.

THE DISCIPLINE OF THE ‘TWO BOYS’

What is remarkable is not simply that stones reportedly flew or that police blocked a road being used by a presidential candidate. What is remarkable is that Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu refused to give the provocation the reaction it appeared capable of producing. They did not turn the convoy around. They did not allow shattered windows, stones or a police blockade to become bigger than the political message they had travelled to deliver.

They proceeded to Mpatamatu and addressed the people who had been waiting for them. Zulu stood before miners, youths and farmers and told them in Bemba that their cries had been heard. Mundubile, rather than spending his speech attacking those accused of trying to prevent him from reaching the rally, pledged to establish a National Miners’ Day to honour the men and women whose labour has helped build Zambia’s economy.

That is discipline, but it is also political calculation. The opposition appears to understand that one angry reaction could change the entire story. A scuffle, a retaliatory stone, a broken window or an exchange with police could quickly provide the excuse to stop a procession, disrupt a rally or portray the opposition itself as the source of disorder.

The opposition therefore finds itself carrying an extraordinary burden. It must campaign, absorb provocation and simultaneously police its own reaction. It must remain calm enough not only to protect its supporters, but also to deny those confronting it the very excuse that could be used to restrict its campaign further.

WHAT PEACE ARE WE TALKING ABOUT?

That is why the President’s own temperament matters. “Nyon’go, Nyon’go, Nyon’go” was directed at Gary Nkombo, not Mundubile or Zulu. But the episode remains relevant because it offered a glimpse of a President appearing increasingly impatient at precisely the moment when Zambia needs presidential restraint most.

When the same Head of State is also reducing political opponents to “boys”, while opposition vehicles are reportedly being damaged and opposition convoys are encountering police blockades, the contrast becomes difficult to ignore. The President may regard some of this language as campaign banter, but presidential words carry a weight that ordinary campaign rhetoric does not. The office requires more.

President Hichilema cannot demand peaceful conduct from everyone beneath him while creating the impression that political pressure is eroding his own patience. He cannot preach restraint while allowing his language to drift towards ridicule. And those entrusted with maintaining law and order cannot allow circumstances to develop in which opposition candidates appear to require extraordinary patience simply to exercise their right to campaign.

The burden of maintaining peace cannot rest on the opposition simply refusing to retaliate. Real peace is not achieved when one side throws a stone and the other side decides not to throw it back. Real peace exists when nobody is allowed to throw the stone in the first place, and when the police stand between competing political forces without fear, favour or partisan appearance.

WHEN THE REACTION SAYS IT ALL

This is where the Mufasa effect becomes politically interesting. Nobody needs to pretend that Mundubile and Zulu have already won anything. Zambians will make that decision themselves on August 13. President Hichilema remains the incumbent and continues to campaign on his government’s record. Elections are decided by voters, not metaphors.

But you do not need to win an election before you begin affecting the behaviour of your opponent. Sometimes you simply need to get into his head. Perhaps the “boys” have brought more to the table than was anticipated. Perhaps Mundubile and Zulu have discovered that refusing to be provoked can itself become a political weapon.

Perhaps the scenes from Kalingalinga to the Copperbelt matter precisely because they allow voters to compare the temperament of those wielding power with the restraint of those seeking it. Government officials have denied wrongdoing in relation to previous incidents, while responsibility for the reported Copperbelt attacks must ultimately be established through proper investigation rather than political accusation. Police had offered no comment on Friday’s reported convoy attack at the time of writing.

But politically, the images already carry their own weight. Zambians vote on August 13. The closer that date gets, the less useful speeches about peace become if the experience on the ground tells another story. Kalingalinga happened. Then came Ndola, the reported attacks on campaign vehicles and the confrontation in Luanshya. Against that background stands a President whose language appears increasingly impatient as the “two boys” he has repeatedly dismissed refuse to disappear.

“Nyon’go, Nyon’go, Nyon’go” was directed at Gary Nkombo, but perhaps its wider significance was the glimpse it offered of a President under pressure. And that is what makes the Mufasa effect interesting.

Mundubile and Zulu do not have to say they are getting under the President’s skin. Sometimes, the reaction says it for them.

World.title: Nkombo Urges President Hichilema to Stay Out of Presidential Contest
World.content:
Independent Mazabuka Central parliamentary candidate Gary Nkombo has advised President Hakainde Hichilema not to be drawn into the contest between the UPND and the Tonse Alliance presidential candidate.

Mr. Nkombo said his focus remains on serving the people of Mazabuka Central and securing his position as Member of Parliament, rather than taking sides in the presidential race.

He said his priority is to address issues affecting residents of Mazabuka Central and continue working for their interests.

Mr. Nkombo’s remarks come amid heightened political activity as various candidates and political parties intensify their campaigns ahead of the elections.

World.title: Brian Mundubela Raises Concern Over Alleged Political Violence in Kitwe
World.content:
Opposition figure Brian Mundubela has questioned whether the reported acts of violence during the campaign period reflect the peace that President Hakainde Hichilema has consistently advocated for.

In a statement, Mr. Mundubela said Zambians should begin to look beyond political rhetoric and assess political parties based on their actions, emphasizing that violence has no place in a democratic society.

The statement follows an alleged incident in Kitwe on the Copperbelt, where Mr. Mundubela and other opposition members were reportedly attacked while conducting campaign activities. He alleged that their members were assaulted, while campaign vehicles were vandalized and stones were thrown during the incident.

Mr. Mundubela called on all political parties to be allowed to campaign freely and peacefully, urging stakeholders to promote tolerance and respect for democratic freedoms ahead of the elections.

He further appealed for political players to uphold peace and ensure that citizens can participate in the electoral process without fear or intimidation.

World.title: President Hichilema assures completion of Monze – Niko Road
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has assured the people of Namwala District of Southern Province that the government will ensure that the construction of Monze – Niko Road is completed on time in order to spur economic development in the district.

And President Hichilema has directed the Road Development Agency RDA to ensure that a roundabout is also constructed on the road to reduce road accidents in the area.

The Head of State has further directed RDA to also work on Namusonde – Mala Road as well as to open up a road that will lead to Itezhi-Tezi District.

President Hichilema said this today when he addressed Namwala residents at Mangwele Primary and Secondary School grounds.

President Hichilema also noted that the government will ensure that Chitingo Livestock Centre is opened in order to vaccinate cattle and protect them from different diseases.

“This road that you are seeing today did not just come from nowhere, we saw the challenges you were facing, and we planned as a government and ensured that the road was constructed and it is here.

“It is now my job to ensure that the road is completed with a roundabout to ensure that no accidents should be recorded as well as construct other roads,” he noted.

On employment, President Hichilema stated that the government has employed teachers and health workers among others to ensure that the living standards of people are uplifted.

President Hichilema also outlined different social protection programmes as well as implementation of the free education policy as some of the interventions that the government will continue to implement once voted back into power on August 13.

“Am urging you to vote for the United Party for National Development (UPND) so that more of such development should continue,” he stated.

The Head of State also noted that farmers supplying their produce to the Food Reserve Agency FRA will be paid upon delivering.

“From today onwards, you will be getting paid immediately you supply your produce to FRA,” he stated.

Meanwhile, UPND Aspiring Candidate for Namwala East, Clara Chibola, and UPND Aspiring candidate for Namwala West, Herbert Mapani, urged Namwala residents to vote for UPND in the forthcoming General Elections for continued development.

The two aspiring candidates noted that the district has registered unprecedented development which needs to be continued, hence the need to vote the UPND back into power.

World.title: Evelyn Hone College holds 59th Graduation Ceremony
World.content:
Government has reaffirmed its commitment to promoting competence-based training and entrepreneurship as key pillars for job creation and sustainable economic growth.

Speaking during the 59th Graduation Ceremony of Evelyn Hone College of Applied Arts and Commerce, Ministry of Technology and Science Permanent Secretary, Brilliant Habeenzu, who was represented by Director of Planning and Information Derrick Saboi, said competence-based education is critical in equipping learners with practical skills required by the labour market.

“Competence-based education is essential in preparing learners for the demands of today’s labour market,” he said.

Dr Habeenzu said the theme of the graduation ceremony, “Promoting Competence-Based Training and Entrepreneurship for Inclusive Sustainable Growth,” reflects government’s agenda of transforming the economy through skills development.

He said competence-based learning enables students to acquire practical skills, critical thinking and problem-solving abilities, ensuring they are ready for employment and self-employment.

Dr Habeenzu noted that countries that have adopted competence-based training have recorded higher youth employment levels and stronger entrepreneurial growth, adding that Zambia should continue investing in practical skills development.

He said government remains committed to supporting skills development through the Skills Development Fund established under the Skills Development Act No. 46 of 2016 to ensure training programmes respond to labour market needs.

Dr Habeenzu added that colleges should position themselves as centres of AI literacy, innovation and applied research to produce graduates capable of driving economic growth.

“Artificial intelligence must become part of our education system to prepare graduates for the future,” he said.

Evelyn Hone College of Applied Arts and Commerce Acting Principal, Charity Nyerongo has urged graduates to embrace competence-based training and entrepreneurship as key drivers of inclusive and sustainable national development.

“Competence-based training bridges the gap between education and industry,” she said.

Ms Nyerongo said the rapidly changing global environment requires graduates to possess not only theoretical knowledge but also practical skills that enable them to address real-world challenges.

He further thanked the government through the Ministry of Technology and Science and the Technical Education, Vocational and Entrepreneurship Training Authority (TEVETA) for its continued support, including expanded bursaries and the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), which has enabled many vulnerable students to access tertiary education.

World.title: ECZ cations against political violence
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has cautioned that political violence could discourage voter participation and undermine confidence in the electoral process ahead of the August 13, 2026 General Elections.

ECZ Chief Electoral Officer, Brown Kasaro, says there is no justification for any form of violence during an election, as candidates and political parties have been given an opportunity to compete peacefully.

Speaking during the 2026 Election Update Programme, Mr Kasaro said isolated incidents of violence had been recorded during the campaign period, with the Police intervening to restore order and deal with alleged perpetrators.

“There is no justification for any form of violence in an election. Candidates and political parties have been given an opportunity to compete, and ultimately, the people will make a choice,” he said.

He noted that the ECZ had, in some instances, suspended campaigns in areas where violence had occurred, adding that the suspensions were lifted once order was restored.

Mr Kasaro said political violence could negatively affect voter participation by creating fear among citizens and preventing them from freely engaging in the electoral process.

He said the Commission had also introduced a presidential campaign timetable to bring order to the campaign process and minimise clashes among competing candidates.

“The objective of the Commission was to bring order to the campaign process of the presidential candidates, and having understood the rationale, the presidential candidates agreed to the arrangement,” Mr Kasaro said.

He said the arrangement had largely helped candidates to campaign in designated areas and reduced the possibility of clashes between them.

Mr Kasaro urged political parties, candidates, civil society organisations and members of the public to promote peaceful campaigns and allow voters to listen to competing messages before making their choice.

He said the ECZ remained open to engaging political parties, civil society organisations, the Church and other stakeholders to address concerns arising during the electoral process.

Meanwhile, Mr Kasaro said the printing of ballot papers had been completed, with the first consignment expected to arrive in Zambia on Sunday, July 26, 2026 and the entire consignment expected before the end of July.

He said the arrival of the ballot papers will be open to observation by political parties, presidential candidates and other accredited stakeholders to enhance transparency in the electoral process.

Mr Kasaro said there would be no surprises during the election, as the number of registered voters, polling stations, candidates and procedures for voting, counting and announcing results were already known.

“The country can be very confident that we are going to oversee a credible election. The ingredients are there, and there will be no surprises because the procedures have been laid out,” he said.

World.title: Govt. hands over agricultural equipment to farmers in Manyinga
World.content:
Government has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening household food security and improving the livelihoods of vulnerable farming households through the Food Security Pack (FSP) Programme, with the handover of agricultural equipment to beneficiaries in Manyinga District.

Speaking when she officiated at the handover ceremony today, District Commissioner, Brenda Mukwakwa, said the event marked another milestone with government’s efforts to empower rural communities and promote sustainable agricultural production.

Ms Mukwakwa said the Ministry of Community Development and Social Services continues to implement several social protection programmes, including the Food Security Pack, Social Cash Transfer, Women’s Livelihood Support and Child Protection Programmes, aimed at reducing poverty and improving the welfare of vulnerable households.

She explained that the Food Security Pack Programme is designed to support poor but viable farming households with agricultural inputs such as fertiliser, seed, livestock and training.

The District Commissioner noted that the programme consists of three components namely the Rain-fed Component, the Wetland Component and the Alternative Livelihood Intervention (ALI), which focuses on livestock production.

She disclosed that in the 2025/2026 farming season, the Rain-fed component alone supported 1,062 beneficiary households in the district.

Ms Mukwakwa said the interventions are intended to enhance household food security, improve income levels and promote better nutrition while helping communities withstand the effects of drought.

She further noted that the government has strengthened management of the Food Security Pack Programme through increased funding, capacity building and investments in programme management systems.

The District Commissioner said the agricultural equipment being handed over will benefit farmers across ten wards in the district.

She said the equipment comprises 14 water pumps, seven maize shellers, five hammer mills and one groundnut sheller, procured at a total cost of K403, 000.

Ms Mukwakwa said the equipment is expected to reduce labour demands, increase agricultural productivity and improve household incomes among small-scale farmers.

She commended Community Welfare Assistance Committees (CWACs), government officers and beneficiaries who have consistently honoured their repayment obligations, saying their commitment has made it possible for the government to reinvest in farming communities.

Ms Mukwakwa further urged beneficiaries to continue contributing the 10 percent payback from their agricultural produce, describing the initiative as essential for sustaining the programme and extending similar support to other communities.

She said the equipment will benefit wards including Chiteve, Kasamba, Chifuwe North, Chongo, Manyinga, Loloma, Kachikenge, Mukosho, Dihamba and Kashinakazhi.

Ms Mukwakwa encouraged beneficiaries to use the equipment responsibly, form cooperatives where possible and prioritise timely repayments to ensure the sustainability of the programme.

She also called on the beneficiaries to safeguard the equipment, saying it belongs to the communities and is intended to improve their livelihoods.

Provincial Senior Community Development Officer, Nancy Ikowa, said the Department of Community Development offers programmes that aim to improve the livelihoods of Manyinga and reduce poverty.

Ms Ikowa further noted that under the Wetlands component, farmers who benefit are those with access to rivers and streams and are given vegetables and maize for farming, while in the Rain-fed component farmers are given fertiliser.

Earlier in his welcoming remarks, Chairperson of the District Food Security Committee, Paul Mwansa, said the handover of the equipment demonstrates government’s commitment to improving food security and building resilient farming communities.

Mr Mwansa, who is the District Agricultural Coordinator, noted that the Food Security Pack Programme continues to empower vulnerable but viable farming households through improved access to productive assets, agricultural inputs and capacity building.

He added that the programme is helping communities increase agricultural production, strengthen household resilience and improve food and nutrition security through collaboration between government and local communities.

Meanwhile, Teddy Kiliyo, Chairperson for Nswanakalezhi Community Welfare Assistance Committees from Kashinakazhi Ward, concluded by thanking President Hakainde Hichilema and the government for their continued commitment to inclusive development.

Mr Kiliyo urged his fellow beneficiaries to ensure the equipment is put to productive use for the benefit of present and future generations.

World.title: ECZ to promote inclusive electoral participation
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has reaffirmed its commitment to promoting inclusive electoral participation for persons with disabilities ahead of the August 13, 2026 general elections.

ECZ Voter Education Programme Manager, Emmah Mwiinga, says the Commission remains committed to ensuring that every eligible citizen participates freely, equally and meaningfully in the electoral process regardless of disability.

Ms Mwiinga was speaking when she officially opened a two-day Lusaka Provincial Workshop on Inclusive Electoral Participation for Persons with Disabilities in Lusaka today.

She noted that persons with disabilities are equal citizens with constitutional rights to register as voters, access electoral information, vote independently and in secrecy and contribute to the country’s democratic governance.

Ms Mwiinga explained that this year general election marks a significant milestone as it will be the first to be conducted under Constitution Amendment Act No. 13 of 2025 and the Electoral Process (Amendment) Act No. 12 of 2026 that introduced the Mixed Member Proportional Representation (MMPR) electoral system and reserved seats for women, youths and persons with disabilities in the National Assembly and local councils.

Ms Mwiinga observed that despite progress made over the years, persons with disabilities continue to face challenges in accessing electoral information and services due to inaccessible polling stations, limited accessible voter education materials, communication barriers, digital exclusion and social stigma.

She disclosed that the Commission has introduced several measures to improve accessibility, including voter education materials in braille and sign language as well as tactile ballot paper jackets, which will be available at all polling stations during the forthcoming elections.

Ms Mwiinga further said the Commission has rolled out disability-inclusive voter education programmes and trained electoral officers on inclusive electoral practices to ensure that no eligible voter is left behind.

She thanked cooperating partners which include Zambia Federation of Disability Organisations (ZAFOD), United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES), for their continued support in strengthening inclusive electoral processes in Zambia.

Meanwhile, ZAFOD Programme Manager, Misheck Katongo has called on ECZ to consider employing persons with disabilities within its staff establishment.

Mr Katongo said meaningful inclusion should go beyond voter participation and extend to employment opportunities for persons with disabilities in electoral institutions.

He further called on the Commission and other stakeholders to move beyond commitments and translate disability inclusion into practical actions that promote equal participation of persons with disabilities in leadership and governance.

The workshop is being held under the theme, “strengthening inclusive electoral participation for persons with disabilities in the 2026 general elections.”
